title: Can Hardwood Be Installed Over Existing Hardwood, Tile or Vinyl?
meta: Can hardwood go over existing hardwood, tile or vinyl? Yes over wood and sheet vinyl, rarely over tile. Snohomish answers from Wills Flooring, $3.25 labor.
keywords: install hardwood over existing hardwood, hardwood over tile, hardwood flooring over vinyl, can you put wood floors over old floors, hardwood installation Snohomish WA
offers: Hardwood floor installation, engineered or solid

blocks.lead: Yes over existing hardwood and over flat, well-stuck sheet vinyl. Usually no over tile: it can be done with a glued or floated engineered floor if the tile is dead flat and sound, but in most Snohomish houses the height, the grout lines and the cracked corners make tear-out the better job.
blocks.detail: Wills Flooring installs engineered or solid hardwood for $3.25 per sq ft and unfinished hardwood for $2.75 per sq ft, 500 sq ft minimum. Tear-out and subfloor prep are quoted at the free in-home estimate after we look at what is down.

blocks.html: Snohomish homeowners are practical people. Whether it is a farmhouse on acreage off Fobes Hill or a 1990s house in Clearview, the question we hear is: "Can you just go over what is there and save me the tear-out?" Sometimes yes, and it saves real money. Sometimes the new floor ends up an inch higher than the kitchen tile and every door drags. Here is how we decide, floor by floor.

blocks.text: Floor by floor: what can be covered

head: Existing floor
Can hardwood go over it?
How
The catch
rows: Solid hardwood, nailed
Yes
Nail or staple new solid or engineered at 45 to 90 degrees to the old boards, or float engineered over a pad
Height rises 1/2 to 3/4 in; loose or cupped old boards must be fastened or replaced first

No
Remove it first; a floating floor under a floating floor moves twice

blocks.text: The height problem nobody prices in

items.title: Doors and thresholds
items.text: New 3/4 inch solid over old 3/4 inch oak raises the floor a full inch above the original height. Interior doors need trimming, exterior doors may not clear at all, and the transition into a tiled bathroom becomes a trip step.

items.title: Appliances and cabinets
items.text: A dishwasher that slid in with 1/4 inch to spare will be trapped by a floor an inch higher. Toe kicks shrink, the range sits low, and a future fridge may not fit under the cabinets. In Snohomish kitchens we often recommend tearing out just the kitchen and going over the rest.

items.title: Stairs
items.text: Raising a floor at the top or bottom of a staircase changes the first riser height, which is a code issue and a tripping hazard. Hardwood on stairs is $125 per stair, and going over an old floor may mean rebuilding that first step.

items.title: Engineered as the answer
items.text: Because engineered hardwood comes in 3/8 and 1/2 inch, it solves most height problems that solid creates. It is also the only sensible option over vinyl or tile since it can be glued or floated instead of nailed.

blocks.title: Check underneath before you cover anything:
blocks.text: Most Snohomish homes sit over a vented crawlspace, and many older farmhouses have damp ones. Covering an old floor traps whatever moisture is coming up through it. We take a moisture reading of the existing floor and the subfloor at every estimate; if the old floor reads above 12 percent, the crawlspace needs a vapor retarder before new wood goes down.

blocks.html: Old fir in downtown Victorians is a special case. It is often the original subfloor and the finish floor at once, with gaps between boards and sometimes a bit of bounce. Nailing new hardwood over it works well and stiffens the house, as long as squeaks and loose boards are screwed down first. Mud and boots come in through the same farm door every day, so the transition where old floor meets new is the spot that fails first; we plan it deliberately.

blocks.text: Go over it or tear it out: a straight comparison

a.title: Makes sense when
items: Old hardwood is sound, flat and nailed, and height is not a problem at doors
Sheet vinyl is flat, stuck down and possibly asbestos-backed, so leaving it is safer
You are installing engineered and can float or glue
Rooms have no tile transitions or appliances to fight

b.title: Makes sense when
items: Tile is anything but perfectly flat and sound
The old floor is a floating laminate or LVP
Existing hardwood is cupped, water damaged or badly loose
The kitchen has cabinets and appliances that cannot take an extra inch

blocks.text: Mistakes we get called to redo

items: Nailing new solid parallel to the old boards. The joints line up, the floor telegraphs every old gap, and it never feels solid. New boards run at an angle or perpendicular to the old ones.
Gluing engineered over tile without grinding the glaze and filling grout lines. The bond holds on the tile surface and fails at every grout line within a year.

blocks.text: What to ask at the estimate

items.html: What is the moisture reading of the existing floor and the crawlspace side? We check both on every hardwood installation estimate in Snohomish.
What will the finished height be at every doorway and appliance? Ask for it in inches, room by room, before you sign.
Is tear-out a separate line? Ours is quoted on site after we see the floor, so the number on the contract is the number you pay.
Who fixes squeaks and loose boards first? Fastening the old floor is part of our prep, and the whole job carries a 1-year workmanship warranty.

faq.q: Can you install hardwood directly over old hardwood floors?
faq.a: Yes, if the old floor is nailed solid, flat and dry. New boards run perpendicular or at 45 degrees to the old ones and are nailed through them into the subfloor. Loose or cupped boards are fastened or replaced first. Expect the finished floor to sit 1/2 to 3/4 inch higher than before.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to install hardwood over an existing floor than to remove it?
faq.a: Usually, because you skip tear-out and disposal. Labor for the hardwood itself is $3.25 per sq ft either way at Wills Flooring. The savings disappear if going over the old floor forces door trimming, threshold rebuilding or kitchen appliance problems, which is why we price both routes at the estimate.

faq.q: Can hardwood be installed over ceramic tile?
faq.a: It is possible with engineered hardwood glued or floated over tile that is completely flat, fully bonded and uncracked, after grinding the glaze and filling grout lines. In practice most Snohomish tile is not flat enough and the added height causes problems, so we usually recommend removing it.

faq.q: What about old sheet vinyl or linoleum in a Snohomish farmhouse?
faq.a: If it is flat and stuck down, engineered hardwood can be floated or glued over it. Vinyl installed before about 1980 may contain asbestos in the backing or adhesive, so leaving it in place and covering it is often the safest option. Never sand or scrape it without testing first.

faq.q: Does the crawlspace matter when covering an old floor?
faq.a: A lot. Covering an old floor traps moisture coming up from a damp crawlspace, and the new hardwood cups by the next wet season. We take moisture readings of the existing floor and subfloor at every Snohomish estimate, and if they read high the crawlspace needs a vapor retarder first.

faq.q: Can I put solid hardwood over a concrete slab?
faq.a: Not directly. Solid hardwood must be nailed into a wood subfloor, so a slab needs a plywood layer first, which adds height and cost. Engineered hardwood glued or floated over a moisture barrier is the practical choice for slabs, garages converted to living space and daylight basements.
